:::note[Written against main]
This page follows `main` at dfb7159, and it differs from the copy in HotLoop Flow 2.5.0, the latest release. Parts of it may be newer than what you have installed. The [release notes](/releases/) say what moved.
:::

It follows your system, light or dark, and each picture below is shown both ways,
light first. Every picture below comes from `web/shots/screenshots.sh`, which starts the real binary
and a real browser, so they get retaken when the editor changes and can't drift
into a mockup. The plant on the canvas is an oven line with two deployments
behind it.

## Wire it, run it, watch it

![The editor on an oven line: the canvas, the deployment history, and the debug and runtime panels](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/editor.png)
![The same, in dark](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/editor-dark.png)

The canvas is what's running. The debug dock under it prints what your debug
nodes see, and the Runtime table beside it counts what went into and out of
every node, with a bar for how full its queue is. When a line misbehaves you
read it off the screen instead of going digging in a log.

## Review it before it reaches the line

![The review panel listing one changed node, with a note box, beside the canvas with that node outlined](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/review.png)
![The same, in dark](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/review-dark.png)

Deploy doesn't deploy. It draws the change on the canvas, writes it out in
words, and asks you for a note. The note lands in the history beside your name,
so whoever gets the call at 2 a.m. can see what changed and why.

## Follow a message down the wires

![A traced message lit across the canvas with the time each node spent on it, and the debug dock below](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/debug.png)
![The same, in dark](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/debug-dark.png)

Click Trace on a debug line and the path that message took lights up across the
canvas, hop by hop, with what each node did to it and how long it took. Turn it
into a test, or replay it into a draft, from the same panel.

## Signing in

![The sign-in card](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/signin.png)
![The same, in dark](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/signin-dark.png)

![The notice a runtime shows when the dashboard signs people in and this page was opened another way](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/dashboard-signin.png)
![The same, in dark](/synced/flow/docs/screenshots/dashboard-signin-dark.png)

It won't start unlocked, so the first thing anyone sees is a sign-in. When the
EmberCORE dashboard signs people in, a runtime opened any other way says to come
in through the dashboard instead of asking for a second password.
